explanation: An agreement or commitment between God and people, often with promises and conditions from both parties.
A religious ritual in which the foreskin of a man's penis is removed as a sign of belonging and submission to God's covenant.
The first patriarch in the Jewish, Christian, and Islamic faiths, formerly known as Abram, who made a covenant with God and was promised many descendants.
Abraham's wife, formerly known as Sarai, who was also part of the covenant and was promised to bear a son despite her old age.
The son of Abraham and Sarah, born when they were old, and regarded as an important figure in Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.
The son of Abraham and Hagar, his Egyptian slave woman, considered the ancestor of the Arabs and an important figure in Islam.
Abraham's Egyptian slave woman who bore him a son, Ishmael, before the covenant with God was made.
The holy name of God in Genesis, often translated as "Lord" or "Yahweh," used to emphasize God's presence and involvement in human life.
